title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter & token/event ordering in SSE streaming
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Multiple customers and internal integrations observed malformed partial-JSON payloads when consuming SSE streaming responses. Root causes: (1) delimiter bytes (

 and token/event separators) were emitted in the wrong order for edge chunking patterns, (2) partial JSON tokens were framed across chunks without deterministic buffering which caused "unexpected end" errors in clients, and (3) token/event ordering could be inverted under tight batching and retry paths. This PR fixes the framing logic in the SSE runtime, adds deterministic buffering for partial JSON payloads, and hardens the token/event ordering guarantees.

Summary of changes: implemented an explicit delimiter-first emission policy (emit delimiter markers before event/token payloads when a boundary is crossed), introduced a small bounded reassembly buffer for partial JSON tokens with clear flush semantics, adjusted the streaming state machine to enforce monotonic token sequence numbers, added unit and integration tests (including a new chunking fuzz harness to simulate network fragmentation), and added a targeted e2e test for tool/function-calling streams to ensure structured output is preserved across streaming boundaries.

Checklist:
- [x] Fix delimiter ordering in runtime/sse/streamer.go
- [x] Add partial-token reassembly buffer and flush semantics
- [x] Unit tests for framing and ordering
- [x] Integration test with simulated network chunking
- [x] Add e2e test for tool-calling structured output over SSE
- [x] Update changelog/release notes

Commits summary: squash of 5 commits: "fix(sse): ensure delimiter emitted before payload on boundary"; "feat(sse): add partial-json reassembly buffer and flush semantics"; "test(sse): add chunking fuzz harness and deterministic chunker"; "test(e2e): tool-calling streaming preserving structured output"; "docs: add note about SSE framing guarantees".

Files changed (high level): runtime/sse/streamer.go (framing + state machine), runtime/sse/streamer_test.go (unit tests), runtime/sse/fuzz_chunker_test.go (fuzz harness), runtime/sse/parser.go (reassembly helpers), sdk/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go (adapter fixes for partial-json tokens), examples/streaming-tool-calls/sample_app.go (e2e test harness), docs/streaming.md (behavior and guarantees), RELEASE_NOTES.md (entry).

CI history: initial CI run showed failures in integration-sse due to the test's non-deterministic chunker exposing a race in the test harness; I updated the test to use a deterministic chunker for CI and kept a fuzz harness for local runs. After the test fix and a small timeout increase in the integration runner the CI passed all checks.

Review notes and discussion: reviewers asked for a clear invariant describing buffering and flush conditions; added extensive comments and a short section in docs/streaming.md. Priya requested an additional e2e that exercises the OpenAI-compatible adapter to verify function-calling JSON objects are never split across events; Diego suggested adding a monotonic token sequence number — implemented as a lightweight per-stream counter to simplify assertions and help debugging. Lucas ran a quick perf microbenchmark and verified ~1% median latency increase for tiny payloads but eliminated several classes of client-visible errors (acceptable tradeoff).

Merge: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-15. Backported critical fixes to release/v1.12 (see branch release/v1.12-sse-fix-430210).
